result.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
result.summary: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts. For coding agents, reproduction success can therefore depend on their ability to fill in missing details, rather than on the released artifacts alone. We ask whether preserving recovered procedures and decisions improves subsequent independent reproduction. We define a standardized artifact design comprising a refined codebase, environment setup, experiment launchers, and a reproduction guide, and introduce ReproBridge, an agent workflow for constructing these refined reproducible artifacts. ReproBridge-Bench provides 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments across 36 papers, anchored by five human-verified reference scores per task. Agents attempt tasks in fresh sessions with raw code or refined artifacts; a separate Auditor checks execution evidence. Across four evaluated models, refined artifacts raise mean reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6% and reduce downstream API spending by 19.7% on average. The cross-model success-rate spread narrows from 21.6 to 3.9 percentage points, with all four models achieving mean success rates above 90%. Removing any component reduces success in the ablation study, with the largest losses from code and environment removal. These results suggest that preserving execution knowledge helps even models with lower raw-code success reproduce experiments more reliably and at lower API cost.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ReproBridge，用编码智能体把论文、代码与辅助材料整理成标准化可复现工件（精炼代码库、环境配置、实验启动脚本、复现指南），并构建含 1029 个任务的 ReproBridge-Bench，另设 Auditor 依据执行证据判定复现是否成功。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「保留已恢复的流程与决策」以及独立 Auditor 依执行证据核验结果的设计，可能与 LVR 中证据核验、停止决策与中间状态保存的评价方式相关，可供核查。
